A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PRISM and retain identifiable methods, experiments and appendices. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the complete documents, including equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original action-recognition experiments on four datasets, cross-architecture evaluations, ablations and qualitative optical-flow analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds action-retrieval, storage-scaling, initialization and sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The stated training objective changes substantially: v1 Eq. (7) matches task-loss gradients and minimizes over model parameters and synthetic videos; v2 Eq. (8) matches class-mean features and minimizes over key frames. The sparse interpolation and insertion framework remains. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects v1's description or reflects an implementation change.

E1.justification: MiniUCF, HMDB51, Kinetics-400 and SSv2 remain the evaluated datasets. V2 adds action retrieval on HMDB51 at 1 VPC, providing a limited extension beyond action recognition without adding a dataset. The 30-VPC experiment changes the budget within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain Random, Herding, K-Center, DM and Wang et al.; cross-architecture comparisons retain DM and Wang et al. The added retrieval comparison also uses Wang et al. No new external comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation against storage percentage, extends PRISM to 30 VPC, and introduces metric-learning evaluation with Recall@1/5/10/20 for retrieval. It also adds threshold and scheduling sweeps and a fully learnable initialization control. Existing benchmark preprocessing, backbones, accuracy metrics and Table A hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds storage-based scaling analysis, a fully learnable initialization ablation, an epsilon sweep and a warm-up/cool-down sensitivity sweep. Conversely, v1's main-text optical-flow comparison and Appendix C optical-flow success/failure analyses are removed. The earlier component ablations and scheduling visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three evaluations and retain the same mean-plus/minus reporting practice in the corresponding accuracy and ablation tables. V2 calls the evaluations independent but supplies no new seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test.

E6.justification: V2 adds 30-VPC accuracies of 34.4% on MiniUCF and 15.6% on HMDB51, retrieval results, and initialization/sensitivity results. Existing values also change: MiniUCF accuracy with three initial frames changes from 16.4±0.5 to 17.3±0.8; full-dataset Kinetics-400/SSv2 accuracies change from 30.3/23.0 to 34.6/29.0; DM storage at 10 VPC changes from 586 to 1150 MB. Main PRISM benchmark and cross-architecture accuracies remain unchanged. Optical-flow findings are removed.

T1.justification: The formal optimization problem is revised from gradient discrepancy to feature-mean discrepancy, including its optimization variables, in v1 Eq. (7) versus v2 Eq. (8). The interpolation mathematics, gradient-misalignment lemma, assumptions and Appendix A proof remain substantively unchanged; renaming the main-text lemma introduces no new theorem.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains holistic, sparse video condensation through gradient-guided frame insertion. V2 narrows the headline accuracy claim from outperforming existing approaches and achieving state-of-the-art results to competitive accuracy with state-of-the-art storage efficiency. The conclusion also drops v1's explicit up-to-70% storage-reduction claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for DM's advantage at Kinetics-400 5 VPC, hypotheses connecting sparse optimization to reduced architecture bias, and interpretations of retrieval, initialization and sensitivity results. Limitations now specify sequences exceeding 16 frames and unexplored generative tasks. V1's optical-flow-specific failure discussion, including problems with nearly motionless endpoints, is removed, while the general abrupt-motion limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 documents fixed-key-set candidate evaluation, simultaneous insertion and subsequent interpolation/gradient recomputation, and clarifies indirect updates to interpolated frames. It omits v1's explicit L2 threshold of 0.141 and detailed random-candidate selection description. Table A's numerical learning rates, batch sizes and evaluation settings are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to DAM: Domain-Aware Module for Multi-Domain Dataset Condensation and Improved Distribution Matching for Dataset Condensation, including brief multi-domain context. The central positioning against Wang et al.'s static/dynamic disentanglement remains, with greater emphasis on fixed-frame redundancy and storage efficiency.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, experimental discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V2 adds an explicit contribution list and experimental-setting subheadings, reorganizes the appendix, relocates limitations, and updates affiliations and acknowledgements. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from one-column to two-column layout, splits v1 Table 1 into small- and large-dataset tables, reverses VPC column ordering and adds storage percentages. It adds an accuracy-compression plot, retrieval and sensitivity tables, and condensed-sequence imagery while removing optical-flow figures. V1 Figures 6–7 are retained as supplementary Figures B–C.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves the mismatch between the stated DM approach and its optimization equation, qualifies the headline accuracy claims, and strengthens evaluation through storage-based comparisons, retrieval transfer and sensitivity tests. These gains are tempered by removal of optical-flow failure evidence and the explicit L2 threshold, alongside unexplained revisions to existing numerical results. The net improvement is supported but limited.
